chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to him: Is there taqiyyah in wiping over the khuffayn? He said: There are three matters in which I do not practice taqiyyah toward anyone: drinking intoxicants, wiping over the khuffayn, and Mutʿat al-Ḥajj.

So this does not contradict the first report regarding the permissibility of taqiyyah in it, because it is possible that the intended meaning in this report is what Zurārah said: for he said, and he did not say, 'It is obligatory upon you not to practice taqiyyah in these toward anyone.' It is also possible that what is meant by it is that there is no taqiyyah in it when the fear does not reach the level of alarm for one’s life or property; in that case, slight hardship should be borne and the khuff should be removed.

key_terms.تَقِيَّةٌ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity practiced out of fear of harm
key_terms.مَسْحِ الْخُفَّيْنِ: wiping over the two leather socks instead of washing the feet in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Is taqiyyah allowed in wiping over the khuffayn during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of taqiyyah in relation to wiping over the khuffayn during wudu (ablution). It states that certain matters are not ordinarily subject to taqiyyah, while the closing explanation reconciles this with other reports by limiting the ruling according to the degree of fear and harm involved.
